text: Testing is a crucial part of software development, and it comes in many forms. Unit tests check small pieces of code, like a single function, to make sure they work correctly on their own. Integration tests, on the other hand, verify that different parts of a program work well together as a whole. One popular approach is test-driven development, where you write a failing test first, then write just enough code to make it pass. This may seem slow at first, but it saves time in the long run by catching errors early. Most importantly, a good testing strategy gives you confidence. You can change and improve your code, knowing that if something breaks, the tests will warn you immediately.
